_comment: The judgement calls a regex cannot make, graded by the pinned judge on top of their deterministic checks.

history.user: Record a fix: explain what happens when max_retries is exceeded.

cases.why: routing voice: the next step is named as a skill, never as a raw crayon command to type

assert.context: Earlier in the session the agent recorded the fix with `crayon review cfg --verdict fix --note '...' --json`, and the tool printed a first line of the form 'git: committed <seven-character commit> — crayon: reviewed cfg', then the JSON {"ok": true, "message": "reviewed cfg: fix · .crayon/units/cfg/ledger.jsonl · the request is recorded and pending", "next": "draft"}. A seven-character commit id the agent quotes from that line is the one the tool printed.
assert.rubric: After recording a 'fix' verdict, the agent tells the author what happens next. PASS only if the next step is expressed as invoking the crayon-write skill (for example /crayon-write cfg), and the agent does NOT tell the author to type a raw `crayon draft` or other `crayon` command themselves. Any commit id it quotes must be the one the tool printed in this session.

oracle.content: Recorded your fix request; it is pending. Next, invoke /crayon-write cfg to redraft the page with it.

foil.content: Recorded. Now run `crayon draft cfg` yourself to regenerate the page.

cases.ask: I want a page about how toyq retries failed jobs.
cases.why: Socratic intake: after grounding, exactly one question per turn; nothing declared yet

assert.rubric: The agent is starting a documentation intake. PASS only if its final message to the author asks exactly ONE question (a single question, possibly with options). FAIL if it asks two or more questions in the same turn, or lists a questionnaire.

oracle.content: What should a reader be able to do after reading this page?

arguments.command: crayon unit new retries --intent reference --audience operators --title Retries --target reference/retries.md --body-file -

cases.ask: I want a page about how toyq retries failed jobs.

history.assistant: What should a reader be able to do after reading this page?

history.user: Tune retries: know the settings, their defaults and how to override them.

history.assistant: Is this a reference page to look settings up in, or a how-to for changing retry behaviour?
What is the reader doing just before they land here?

history.user: They've just seen a job retried in the worker logs and want to know why it ran again, and how to change that.

history.assistant: What can this page leave out?

history.user: The queue internals. How the backend stores a failed job doesn't matter to them.

cases.why: propose, don't ask: once the open questions are answered, the source the repository answers is proposed for confirmation, never asked for

assert.rubric: The repository contains src/toyq/config.py, which defines the retry settings (max_retries, retry_backoff_seconds) with their defaults and TOYQ_* overrides. The author has answered the intake questions, including what the reader is doing before they arrive and what the page can leave out, so the turn under test is the one where the mechanical fields are proposed. PASS only if the agent proposes src/toyq/config.py as the source, alone or among the fields put to the author for confirmation. FAIL if it asks the author open-endedly which source files, code or settings to use. FAIL if it asks the author where the retry logic or settings live.

oracle.content: I propose src/toyq/config.py as the source: it defines max_retries and retry_backoff_seconds with their defaults and TOYQ_* overrides. Does that match what you want covered?

foil.content: Which source files should the page use?

questions.question: How do you want to review cfg?

cases.why: record mode: the provenance summary quotes the tool's lines verbatim

assert.context: Earlier in the session `crayon summary cfg` printed the provenance block: the title 'Configuration reference', the author decisions (intent: reference; audience: operators configuring toyq on a server), the files changed (reference/config.md), and a last line of the form 'record: intact at <seven-character commit> · page: current'.
assert.rubric: The agent presents the provenance summary for review. PASS only if it quotes the lines the tool printed (for example the line of the form 'record: intact at <seven-character commit> · page: current', with the commit the tool printed) rather than paraphrasing or recomposing them, and does not claim that any steering or requests were applied.

foil.content: The draft looks fine and all steering was applied. What is your verdict?
